qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Brand awareness and bundled auto-home inertia provide mild customer stickiness, but personal lines insurance remains a heavily shopped, price-sensitive commodity without an insurmountable economic barrier. 10-year median ROIC of 10.5% fails the 12% hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). While Allstate benefits from customer inertia and brand recognition in personal lines, personal auto and homeowners insurance are highly shopped, price-sensitive products subject to stringent state Department of Insurance rate regulation. 10-year median ROIC of 10.5% falls short of the 12% hurdle. Massive underwriting losses in 2022-2023 (combined ratios of 106.6% and 104.5%) and persistent multi-billion dollar catastrophe losses ($4.96B-$5.63B annually) highlight cyclical vulnerability. Aggressive rate hikes to restore underwriting margins triggered policyholder attrition and market share losses to Progressive.
qualitative.evidence: Empirical financial record confirms sub-hurdle capital efficiency and lack of unconstrained pricing power: (1) Multi-Cycle Returns: 10-year median ROIC is 10.5% (below the 12.0% requirement). While 2024-2025 staged a sharp cyclical recovery (ROE >25-35%, combined ratio 94.3 in 2024 and 85.2 in 2025), full-cycle profitability remains constrained by severe underwriting swings. (2) Underwriting Volatility: Suffered consecutive annual net losses in 2022 (-$1.42B) and 2023 (-$316M) driven by rapid auto parts/medical inflation and extreme weather events. Catastrophe losses totaled $3.11B (2022), $5.63B (2023), $4.96B (2024), and $4.96B (2025). (3) Pricing Power & Regulatory Friction: P&C rate increases require prior state regulatory approval (e.g., CA, NY, NJ), creating substantial margin lag during inflationary spikes. (4) Competitive Disadvantage: Captive/independent agency distribution carries structural cost headwinds relative to direct-to-consumer peers. Countrywide market share sits at ~5.3-5.5%, ceding volume to Progressive (~7.5-8.0%) during rate catch-up cycles.
